sonnet.problem: This is a which-thing question (what name). The wrong answers 'The LORD Our Shepherd' and 'The LORD Our Fortress' are invented names. They are not real details from elsewhere in the Bible.
sonnet.rule: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

sonnet.problem: Verse 20-21 gives a case: 'If you can break My covenant with the day and… the night… then My covenant may also be broken with David.' The question turns it into 'could be broken only if', which says more than the text does.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answer 'The dust of the earth' is a close match for 'the sand on the seashore'. Both are well-known images of countless descendants (Genesis 13:16), so a baker could argue it is right.
sonnet.rule: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
